notes: ABox revision on has_paternal_grandfather, a derived fact worked out from two stored ones (Charles is William's father, Philip is Charles's father): Prince William's paternal grandfather was George VI instead of Prince Philip. The exact phrase is almost absent from the corpus (1, 2 and 30 hits), though Wikipedia uses it once. The related question asks about a different person reached through the grandfather: his wife (Queen Elizabeth II, then Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother), a 2-hop composition; the inverse reading (was Philip a grandfather of William) was dropped because it restates the edit. Derived: a binding (the paternal grandfather of Prince George's father), two compositions (the grandfather's death year, whether he was a king) and a premise-route question reaching William as Prince George's father. The indeterminate question asks Charles III's father (w1 Philip, w2 George VI); w1 is also the answer of a model that did not edit. Caveat: George VI is William's real great-grandfather and had no sons, so neither world is fully coherent.
